review_cost.rationale: Approve-with-changes territory: the fixes are small, local and mechanical (cache eviction, one extracted helper, two guard fixes, some payload types); nothing requires rearchitecting or touches risky code paths.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache Map is never swept: expired entries stay forever and are only removed on fetch rejection. A crawl across all 1,025 Pokémon pages and every version group's moves can accumulate tens of thousands of parsed-JSON entries.
findings.suggestion: Evict expired entries on read/write (the `expires` timestamp is already stored) or cap the map with a simple LRU bound.

findings.issue: The AbortController + fetch + DOMParser + innerHTML-swap helper is duplicated almost line-for-line in components/MoveTables.astro:119-131; the two copies will drift when one is fixed.
findings.suggestion: Extract one shared client helper (e.g. src/lib/swap.ts exporting swapRegion(url, selector)) used by both scripts.

findings.issue: Non-null assertions on document.querySelector mean a markup rename throws at module init and silently disables search, filters and pagination; the twin script in MoveTables.astro uses optional chaining, so the two are inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Guard with `if (!form) return;` or optional chaining, matching MoveTables.astro.

findings.issue: The popstate handler only syncs the Game select when the ?game parameter is present, so back-navigating to a URL without ?game loads the default game's tables but leaves the old game's label selected.
findings.suggestion: Set select.value to the fetched document's selected option (or reset to the default) on popstate, as index.astro's syncForm does for the home filters.

findings.issue: All API payloads are typed `any` (getJson<T = any>, and pages cast records with `(a: any)`), so the strict tsconfig provides no safety on the app's main data path.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the API records actually used (Named, TypeRecord, MoveRecord, PokemonRecord) and annotate getJson calls.

findings.issue: A non-OK, non-404 upstream response throws inside page frontmatter with no handling, producing a bare 500 error page for a transient API hiccup.
findings.suggestion: Catch at the page level (or retry once in getJson) and fall back to a friendly error page; the 60s cache makes a single retry cheap.

findings.issue: All 452 lines of styling live in one global stylesheet instead of Astro's default scoped component styles, so component markup and its CSS live far apart and selectors rely on naming discipline alone.
findings.suggestion: At minimum split per-component sections into the corresponding .astro files as scoped styles; keep the token-heavy base rules in global.css.

summary: A genuinely current, idiomatic Astro 7 SSR app: correct adapter setup, frontmatter data loading, proper 404 handling on every dynamic route and tidy, well-commented modules. The main merge blockers are an unbounded response cache and a duplicated client-side fetch-and-swap helper duplicated across two scripts, plus scattered `any` typing that negates the strict tsconfig. I'd approve after one mechanical round of fixes.
